name: eufy X10 Pro Omni (US)

radios.note: The manual asks for the 2.4 GHz band on your router; disable 5 GHz on dual-band routers during setup.

matter.note: Matter Alpha, a third-party directory, lists the X10 Pro Omni as Matter 1.4 over Wi-Fi with firmware 3.0. No eufy page or CSA listing seen, so not claimed.

apple_home.note: No eufy page found for Apple Home.

google_home.note: eufy's US page lists Google Home as a compatible device and Google Assistant voice control.

alexa.note: eufy's US page lists Amazon Echo as a compatible device and Alexa voice control.

smartthings.note: No eufy or Samsung page found for SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: No official Home Assistant integration page found; only community integrations.

hubRequired.note: The Omni station is not a hub.

localControl.note: eufy says obstacle recognition runs offline; local-only control is not stated.

cleaning.note: Vacuums and mops with spinning pads (MopMaster).

navigation.note: The manual lists a navigation lidar; eufy calls it iPath Laser Navigation. Obstacle avoidance uses a camera (AI.See).

selfEmptying.note: The Omni station empties the bin into a 2.5 L dust bag.

summary: eufy's US page marks the X10 Pro Omni as no longer available, so this matters mostly if you already own one or find it second-hand. It works with Google Home and Alexa, vacuums and mops with 8,000 Pa suction and laser navigation, and its Omni station empties the bin into a 2.5 L dust bag.
caveats: No longer sold on eufy's US page.
Setup needs the 2.4 GHz band; eufy's manual says to turn off 5 GHz on dual-band routers.
A third-party directory lists Matter over Wi-Fi, but no eufy page or CSA listing backs it, so Apple Home isn't confirmed.
Home Assistant has only community integrations for this model, no official one.
